dataSplit.scalingStrategy: StandardScaler fitted strictly within training folds (zero data leakage)

models.description: Bootstrap ensemble of 100 balanced decision trees reducing variance and capturing feature interactions.
Radial Basis Function (RBF) margin maximizer with balanced class penalization and Platt probability scaling.
CART decision tree with balanced class weighting and controlled depth to prevent severe overfitting.
L2-regularized logistic regression with balanced class weighting for inverse frequency calibration.
Sequential gradient-boosted decision trees fitted with balanced inverse-frequency sample weights.

baseline.interpretation: A naive majority classifier predicting Good Standing for every student achieves 97.7% accuracy but flags 0% of at-risk students (Recall = 0.0, Macro-F1 = 0.4942). This demonstrates why Macro-F1 and At-Risk Recall are the only statistically defensible criteria for academic early intervention.

selectedModel.selectionCriterion: Highest Cross-Validated Macro-F1 with Secondary At-Risk Recall Tie-Break
selectedModel.rationale: Random Forest Classifier is selected as the optimal model based on the pre-registered scientific criterion: it achieved the highest Cross-Validated Macro-F1 (0.7370) across 5 stratified folds on the training partition, outperforming Support Vector Machine (RBF) (0.7254, Δ = +0.0116). Crucially, it maintained a strong At-Risk Recall of 93.0% during cross-validation, significantly improving over the trivial majority baseline (Macro-F1: 0.4942, Recall: 0.0%).
selectedModel.tradeoffAnalysis: In the untouched held-out test cohort (N = 964, 22 positive at-risk students), Random Forest Classifier successfully identified 21 out of 22 students in academic deficit (Recall: 95.5%), with only 1 false negative. While its precision is 34.4% resulting in 40 false positive alerts, this trade-off is institutionally sound: the cost of failing to identify a student who requires academic remediation (Type II error) is far more severe than offering academic advising to a student who ultimately succeeds (Type I error).
selectedModel.limitations: 1. Model predictions are diagnostic recommendations, not deterministic judgments. 2. False positives (40 students) should undergo departmental advisory review before intervention. 3. Feature weights reflect longitudinal correlation with historical academic facts, not causal mechanisms. 4. The pipeline should be re-evaluated each academic semester as student cohort distributions evolve.
